Pacioli Labs, Inc. (the "Company," the "Issuer," "we," "us" or "our") was formed in Delaware on September 30, 2026. On that date, we entered into a license agreement with Auditchain Labs AG ("Auditchain"). Auditchain is organized in Switzerland and is an affiliate under common control with us. Jason Meyers, our Chief Executive Officer, controls both Auditchain and us. Under the license agreement, Auditchain granted us a perpetual, global and exclusive license to the Pacioli.ai™ software (the "Auditchain License"). The Auditchain License gives us the right to sublicense the software to any third party.

The Pacioli.ai™ software consists of LucaSuite™, the Pacioli Validating Node software, the Pacioli smart contracts (the "Smart Contracts") and the Pacioli Explorer. We refer to this software as a whole as "Pacioli." The Pacioli Validating Node software includes the Pacioli AI Agent (the "Agent"), which is described under "Material aspects of the associated crypto application." We refer to any person that uses Pacioli as a "User." Pacioli is infrastructure for the preparation and validation of regulatory disclosures. It serves issuers and servicers of crypto assets that are obligated to prepare disclosures in machine-readable form and to file them with regulatory agencies under emerging regulatory frameworks for crypto assets. Those frameworks include the GENIUS Act and Regulation Crypto Assets ("Reg CA") of the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "Commission") in the United States, and the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation ("MiCAR") in the European Union. The Pacioli Explorer is built to give anyone one place to see the validated disclosures of issuers under Reg CA, the GENIUS Act and MiCAR, with a color-coded indicator of compliance for each, the PVNs and MCVs that stand behind it and its on-chain proof. Our aim is for it to become the global destination for disclosure and analysis.

Auditchain began developing Pacioli in 2021 and launched a minimally viable onchain version in November 2024. Pacioli is currently commercially available as a cloud-based software-as-a-service application. We have offered that service since April 5, 2027, when the Auditchain License became effective. Before that date, Auditchain offered it. Auditchain has also used Pacioli to create proposed machine-readable reporting taxonomies and frameworks, such as the framework used to prepare this document, in response to public requests for comment by regulators.

The Network. In its decentralized form, Pacioli runs on a network of nodes (the "Network"). Two kinds of nodes operate on the Network. Pacioli Validating Nodes (each, a "PVN" and together, the "PVNs") validate machine-readable regulatory disclosures. Master conformance validators (each, an "MCV" and together, the "MCVs") are standard setters that specify data and taxonomy formats. Each MCV acts through one or more qualified delegates that it names. The MCVs test whether each PVN conforms to the logic, data format and taxonomy specifications that apply to PVNs and to the disclosures that PVNs validate (the "Technical Specifications"). We refer to each test of a PVN by the MCVs as a "Conformance Validation." A PVN is admitted to the Network only after it passes a Conformance Validation, and it must undergo a Conformance Validation each year. Each person that operates a PVN (an "Operator") pays the MCVs an annual fee for Conformance Validations (the "Conformance Fee") and a separate fee for the first Conformance Validation of its PVN. The MCVs set those fees and publish them. We do not set them, and this document does not state their amounts. Two standard setters serve as the initial MCVs. We refer to an issuer of crypto assets, or an advisor acting for an issuer, that prepares disclosures in Pacioli as a "Preparer." A User may put a request for validation to the whole Network (the "open protocol") or to a private group of PVNs that it engages in place of the whole Network (a "cohort").

AUDT and the Smart Contracts. The subject crypto asset is the AUDT token ("AUDT"), a new ERC20 token. We refer to the Ethereum, Polygon PoS and Robinhood Chain blockchain networks, on which AUDT is or will be deployed, as the "Underlying Networks." AUDT has a maximum supply of 300,000,000, which the Token Contract enforces, and is minted as it is distributed. AUDT is not listed on any trading venue. The Smart Contracts include the AUDT token contract (the "Token Contract"), the validation contract (the "Validation Contract"), the claims contract (the "Claims Contract") and a contract (the "Subsidies Contract") that pays a portion of the rewards for validation work as subsidies ("AUDT Subsidies"). They also include the validator staking contract, the release contract, the engagement contract and the slash contract, which are described under "Material aspects of the associated crypto network," and the multi-signature contract described below. Four further Smart Contracts will be deployed later than the others. They are the network governance contract (the "Governance Contract") and three contracts that are defined below. Unless we state otherwise, a reference in this document to the deployment of the Smart Contracts does not include those four contracts. The addresses of the Smart Contracts are stated under "Material aspects of the associated crypto network" and are to be published at https://pacioli.ai.

Our offerings. We sell units of a covered investment contract, as that term is defined in Rule 100 of Reg CA (a "CIC"). We have structured our capital raising under Reg CA as three offerings. The first is an offering of 70 units of the CIC under the startup exemption of Reg CA (the "Startup Offering"). The second is a Tier 2 offering of 670 units of the CIC under the fundraising exemption of Reg CA (the "Tier 2 Node Offering" and, together with the Startup Offering, the "Node Offerings"). In the Node Offerings, each unit of the CIC is a PVN (a "Unit"). A Unit consists of 50,000 AUDT, delivered staked, together with a license to the Pacioli Validating Node software and the right to operate it on the Network. We refer to that license and that right together as the "Node License." We refer to the machine-readable disclosure models for Reg CA, the GENIUS Act and MiCAR as the "Disclosure Models" and to the disclosure model for Reg CA as the "Reg CA Disclosure Model." The Auditchain License covers the Disclosure Models. A Unit may not be divided, and the AUDT and the Node License in a Unit may not be separated, with two exceptions, which are described under "Material terms of the covered investment contract." An additional Unit that an Operator purchases under the second exception is not a PVN. The third offering, which we intend to make, is a Tier 2 offering of 22,083,333 AUDT, without a PVN or a Node License, under the fundraising exemption of Reg CA (the "Tier 2 AUDT Offering"). We have not filed an offering statement for the Tier 2 AUDT Offering.

This offering circular relates to the Tier 2 Node Offering, which we also refer to as this "Offering." Harrow Street Securities LLC is our placement agent (the "Placement Agent"). It acted in the Startup Offering and acts in the Tier 2 Node Offering. The Auditchain License became effective on April 5, 2027, at the first closing of the Startup Offering.

Other defined terms. When our promised essential managerial efforts are complete, we intend to file a transition report on Form TR under Reg CA ("Form TR"). We refer to the first 30 PVNs admitted to the Network, not counting any PVN that we operate, as the "Founding PVNs." We refer to a regulatory reporting requirement that is carried on the Network, together with its machine-readable disclosure model, its rules and its tests, as a "reporting scheme."

Until we give up our keys to the Smart Contracts, a multi-signature contract holds them (the "Key Holder Contract"). It has five key holders. We are one, and the other four are Operators of Founding PVNs that are not affiliated with us. We refer to the five as the "Initial Key Holders." We refer to the acts by which we give up those keys, immediately before we file Form TR, as the "Handover." The right to change the settings of the Smart Contracts is not one of those keys. We hold it alone. Our right to change the division of each validation fee among its recipients, the amount of the rewards paid through AUDT Subsidies and the allocation of the proceeds from data subscriptions (together, the "allocation of rewards") ends when the Governance Contract is deployed. Our right to change the other settings ends at the Handover. We refer to the signal that we give in the Smart Contracts immediately before we file Form TR, and that opens the functions that wait for that filing, as the "Form TR Signal." The Key Holder Contract, the Handover and the Form TR Signal are described under "Smart contract governance mechanisms."

We refer to a vote of the holders of AUDT on a proposal that is submitted through the Governance Contract as a "Governance Vote." We refer to the council whose approval every proposal also requires as the "Governance Council." Neither we nor Auditchain, nor any person connected with either of us as described under "Governance mechanisms," may hold a seat on it. The Governance Council records its decisions in a contract (the "Council Contract"). The Governance Contract names one address that can cancel a proposal before it is executed (the "Guardian"), and that address is the Council Contract. We refer to the registry in which reporting schemes are filed as the "Scheme Registry," and to the contract in which persons that comment on a reporting scheme lock AUDT as the "Consultation Stake Contract." After the filing of Form TR, the Governance Council may also direct the Subsidies Contract to pay rewards to such persons. The Council Contract, the Scheme Registry and the Consultation Stake Contract are the three further Smart Contracts mentioned above. Governance Votes, the Governance Council and the rules for reporting schemes are described under "Governance mechanisms."

We refer to the security audit by Ironvault Security Labs of the PVN software and of the Smart Contracts, other than the four further Smart Contracts, as the "Security Audit." We refer to the Securities Act of 1933 as the "Securities Act." An "Accredited Investor" is an accredited investor as defined in Rule 501 of Regulation D under the Securities Act (17 CFR 230.501). An "LEI" is a Legal Entity Identifier. A "vLEI" is a verifiable LEI credential. Unless we state otherwise, a reference in this document to a "Rule" is a reference to a rule of Reg CA as proposed.

Purpose of this Offering. We make this Offering primarily to two groups. The first is providers of regulatory disclosure management software and services. The second is issuers of crypto assets that will be required to comply with the technical disclosure specifications under Reg CA and other global standard machine-readable reporting schemes. Each purchaser of a Unit becomes an Operator. We will use the proceeds of this Offering to complete the decentralization of Pacioli and to accelerate its adoption. In this document, the "decentralization" of Pacioli means the completion of the six essential managerial efforts that are set out in the table of essential managerial efforts. It has no other meaning. We believe that a decentralized Pacioli will modernize global regulatory disclosure, will meet the demands of the mass migration of the global capital markets onchain, and will make disclosure preparation and validation available 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

Current status. The Startup Offering, which began on March 1, 2027, is complete. We sold all 70 Units at five closings, the last on August 27, 2027, and delivered 3,500,000 AUDT staked (see the table of the offering in the previous 12 months on the cover page). On April 5, 2027, we allocated 250,000 AUDT to each of the two initial MCVs. Ironvault Security Labs completed the Security Audit on June 15, 2027. On July 1, 2027, we deployed the Smart Contracts on Ethereum and a bridged Token Contract on Polygon PoS, and the AUDT allocated to the MCVs was minted and staked.

By August 31, 2027, the Subsidies Contract had paid AUDT Subsidies of 100,000 AUDT to the PVNs on the Network. It can pay no more than 1,000,000 AUDT before the filing of Form TR, and we intend it to pay the remaining 900,000 AUDT over the period until that filing, split equally each month among the active PVNs, as described under "Plan of development." After the $3,500,000 of sales and the $500,000 allocation to the MCVs, those 1,000,000 AUDT take up the rest of the $5,000,000 limit of the startup exemption. We have not awarded any right to claim AUDT from the team or advisor allocations.

By August 31, 2027, the Founding PVNs had been admitted to the Network after Conformance Validation, and the Network went live on that date. Including our own PVN, 31 PVNs are active. Each of the two MCVs also operates a node. The number of active nodes that we report counts PVNs only. The PVNs of the other 40 Units sold in the Startup Offering have not yet been admitted to the Network.

Five of the six essential managerial efforts that we promised in our Form 1-SU are complete. The remaining effort, which ends with the Handover, is in progress. Its completion is the trigger for Form TR.

At the date of this offering circular, 4,150,000 AUDT is outstanding. Persons other than us hold 4,096,774 AUDT: 3,500,000 AUDT sold in the Startup Offering, 500,000 AUDT allocated to the MCVs and 96,774 AUDT paid as AUDT Subsidies. We hold the other 53,226 AUDT: the 50,000 AUDT from the treasury allocation that we have staked for our PVN and 3,226 AUDT of AUDT Subsidies paid to our PVN.

We activated our Ethereum validator on August 20, 2027. Our application for a Polygon PoS validator and our Robinhood Chain full node will follow.

This Offering consists of 670 Units at a price of $62,500 per Unit, for an aggregate offering price of $41,875,000. Under Rule 101(e)(2) as proposed, that price is the equivalent of $1.25 per AUDT.

The CIC in this Offering is sold in Units. Each Unit is a PVN and consists of the following, which are sold together:

(1) 50,000 AUDT, delivered staked to the purchaser's PVN and locked for a minimum of two years from delivery; and

(2) a Node License.

The Node License is the means by which the AUDT invokes the functions of Pacioli. The PVN software is the software that the AUDT stake activates. Except in the cases described below, neither the AUDT stake nor the Node License has a use without the other.

The Node License is the license to the PVN software, which includes the Agent, and the right to operate that software on the Network. Under the Node License, an Operator may run in production any version of the PVN software that passes Conformance Validation, whoever changed the code, and may validate disclosures under every reporting scheme that the Network carries, without a further license from us or Auditchain and without a further charge by either of us. Neither we nor Auditchain can withdraw those rights while the PVN is staked. The Node License ends when the Operator unstakes. It does not cover LucaSuite™.

A Unit may not be divided. In this Offering, we do not sell AUDT other than as part of a Unit, or in any amount other than the 50,000 AUDT in a Unit. The AUDT and the Node License in a Unit may not be separated, with two exceptions.

First, a provider of regulatory disclosure management software or services may purchase a Unit without the Node License if it (i) operates its PVN with its own software, (ii) complies with the Technical Specifications and (iii) submits to the Conformance Validations performed by the MCVs. A Unit purchased under this exception consists of 50,000 AUDT locked in the validator staking contract. The purchaser may validate disclosures under every reporting scheme that the Network carries, without a license from us or Auditchain and without a charge by either of us. The purchase price per Unit does not change, because no part of the purchase price is allocated to the Node License. All other terms of the Unit, and all obligations of the purchaser, are the same, with one addition. A Unit purchased under this exception may be resold only to a provider of regulatory disclosure management software or services that meets the same three conditions. The MCVs confirm that the buyer meets those conditions when they perform the new Conformance Validation.

Second, an Operator may purchase an additional Unit without the Node License in a Node Offering that is open, for either of two purposes: to restore the stake of its PVN after a penalty, or to stake AUDT for the Preparer discount. An additional Unit consists of 50,000 AUDT, delivered staked and locked for two years, at the price of a Unit. It does not count as a PVN for any purpose: it carries no Conformance Validation, no Conformance Fee and no vote that belongs to a PVN. Its AUDT is applied first to restore the stake of the PVN of the Operator to 50,000 AUDT, and the remainder is staked for the Operator and counts toward the Preparer discount. An additional Unit is one of the Units offered in that Node Offering and does not increase their number. An additional Unit cannot be resold as a Unit. The AUDT that restores the stake becomes part of the stake of the PVN, and the remainder is locked and released on the same terms as AUDT staked for the Preparer discount.

A purchaser may sell a Unit after two years, subject to two conditions. First, a new Conformance Validation of the PVN must be completed before the sale settles. Second, the buyer must be an Accredited Investor that holds an LEI, if the buyer is an entity, or a vLEI that we have issued, if the buyer is an individual. The parties may agree to the sale while the Conformance Validation is pending, and the sale settles when the Conformance Validation is complete. The two-year lock restarts for the buyer. We do not approve transfers and have no discretion over them. The provider of the identity verification (KYC/AML) service performs the identity and accreditation checks.

An individual who operates a PVN must hold a vLEI that we issue under our own LEI. We must issue a vLEI to every individual who completes identity verification (KYC/AML). We may refuse or revoke a vLEI only if the individual fails identity verification or ceases to operate a PVN, or if an order of a court or of a regulator, or a rule of the vLEI system, requires it. We will continue to issue vLEIs on these terms after the filing of Form TR.

Transfers of AUDT from one wallet to another are locked until the day named in the Form TR Signal, as described under "Other material terms of the covered investment contract."

Rule 100 as proposed defines a CIC as an investment contract to which a crypto asset that is not a security is subject and to which no other asset is subject. A Unit that is sold with the Node License includes that license. In Request for Comment 6, the Commission asks whether the definition should permit an investment contract that involves other assets as well.

Under Rule 101(e)(1) as proposed, one unit of a CIC would be one AUDT. For that reason, we report the Rule 101(e) measures alongside our Units. Those measures are the number of AUDT per Unit, the equivalent number of AUDT offered and the equivalent price per AUDT. They allow this Offering to be read either way. In its comment letter on proposed Reg CA (Requests for Comment 6, 7 and 31), Auditchain recommends that the definition permit a functional asset such as the Node License, and that an issuer be permitted to define the unit of a CIC as a functional unit of this kind, with any price allocation disclosed. That would allow institutions to establish a network that includes the software that the crypto asset activates.

No part of the purchase price is allocated to the Node License. The purchase price does not include the initial Conformance Validation of the PVN, which the purchaser pays for separately (see "Purchaser obligations under the covered investment contract").

Each purchaser of a Unit becomes an Operator and has the following obligations.

(1) Accredited Investor. The purchaser must be an Accredited Investor.

(2) Identity. The purchaser must complete identity verification (KYC/AML). A purchaser that is an entity must hold an LEI. An individual who operates a PVN must hold a vLEI that we issue, as described under "Material terms of the covered investment contract."

(3) Conformance Validation. The PVN must pass an initial Conformance Validation before it is admitted to the Network. The PVN must undergo a Conformance Validation each year after that. The annual Conformance Validation covers every reporting scheme that the Network then carries. A PVN is not tested separately for an additional reporting scheme.

(4) Fees of the MCVs. The Operator must pay the MCVs a fee for the initial Conformance Validation and a Conformance Fee each year. A new Conformance Validation on the sale of a Unit also carries a fee. The MCVs set those fees and publish them. We do not set them, and this document does not state their amounts. None of these fees is included in the purchase price of a Unit.

(5) Staking. The Operator must keep the 50,000 AUDT delivered with the PVN staked for a minimum of two years from delivery. If the Operator unstakes, the PVN is deactivated immediately and the Node License ends. The former Operator then claims the stake from the release contract in equal daily amounts over two years.

(6) Slashing. The Operator must accept slashing of the stake in two cases. First, a PVN that does not undergo its annual Conformance Validation forfeits 10 percent of its existing stake. Second, a PVN that withdraws from a validation request after committing to it forfeits 10 percent of its stake on the first withdrawal and 20 percent on the second withdrawal. On each further withdrawal, it forfeits 30 percent and is deactivated for 30 days. The Operator must then restore the stake. The Smart Contracts set no deadline for doing so, and the PVN continues to operate with the reduced stake. The full schedule, the cases in which a PVN is deactivated and the ways in which a stake is restored are described under "Other material terms of the covered investment contract."

(7) Transfer. The Operator may not transfer the Unit within two years after delivery of the AUDT. A sale after those two years is subject to two conditions. A new Conformance Validation of the PVN must be completed before the sale settles, and the buyer must be an Accredited Investor that holds an LEI or a vLEI. The sale does not require our approval. The two-year lock restarts for the buyer.

A purchaser that buys a Unit without the Node License under the first exception has the same obligations. In addition, that purchaser may resell the Unit only to a provider of regulatory disclosure management software or services that meets the three conditions of that exception, which is described under "Material terms of the covered investment contract."
xbrli:xbrl.regca:ConditionsToCoveredInvestmentContr:

The AUDT and the Node License in a Unit may not be separated, except as described under "Material terms of the covered investment contract."

(2) Delivery of the AUDT. We deployed the Smart Contracts on July 1, 2027, after the Security Audit. For Units sold before that date, we delivered the AUDT staked on that date. For Units sold after that date, we deliver the AUDT staked at the closing of the purchase.

(4) Admission. A PVN is admitted to the Network only after it passes a Conformance Validation. Until a PVN is admitted, it cannot validate disclosures on the Network. The two-year lock runs from the delivery of the AUDT, whether or not the PVN has been admitted.

(5) Lock and transfer. The AUDT delivered with a PVN is staked and locked for a minimum of two years from delivery. A purchaser may sell a Unit after two years, subject to two conditions. A new Conformance Validation of the PVN must be completed before the sale settles. The buyer must be an Accredited Investor that holds an LEI, if the buyer is an entity, or a vLEI that we have issued, if the buyer is an individual. The two-year lock then restarts for the buyer. xbrli:xbrl.regca:OtherMaterialTermsOfCoveredInvestm:
Slashing schedule. A PVN that does not undergo its annual Conformance Validation forfeits 10 percent of its existing stake. A PVN is not penalized if its Operator requested the Conformance Validation and paid the Conformance Fee at least 30 days before it was due and the MCVs performed it late. A PVN that undergoes its annual Conformance Validation and does not pass it forfeits nothing. Its Operator has 30 days from the result to cure the deficiencies, and the PVN continues to operate during that time. If the deficiencies are not cured within the 30 days, the MCVs deactivate the PVN. Its stake remains subject to the two-year lock, and the PVN is reactivated when it passes a new Conformance Validation. A PVN that withdraws from a validation request after committing to it forfeits 10 percent of its stake on the first withdrawal, 20 percent on the second withdrawal and 30 percent on each further withdrawal. Each further withdrawal also results in the deactivation of the PVN for 30 days. A separate slash contract administers the forfeitures. It allocates 50 percent of the AUDT forfeited to AUDT Subsidies and 50 percent to the MCVs. It holds the first half and pays it out as AUDT Subsidies only after the Form TR Signal has taken effect.

Restoring a stake. An Operator whose stake has been reduced by a penalty must restore it. The Operator may do so with AUDT that it has earned on the Network, by purchasing an additional Unit without the Node License in a Node Offering that is open, or by purchasing AUDT in the Tier 2 AUDT Offering while it is open. AUDT that an Operator purchases in the Tier 2 AUDT Offering for that purpose, or to stake for the Preparer discount, will be delivered into the stake in full, without the release schedule of that offering, and locked for two years. The Smart Contracts set no deadline for restoring a stake, and the PVN continues to operate with the reduced stake. From the end of the Tier 2 AUDT Offering until transfers of AUDT open, no AUDT can be bought. After transfers of AUDT open, AUDT may cost more.

Release schedule on unstaking. When an Operator unstakes, the Node License ends and the former Operator claims the stake from the release contract in equal daily amounts over two years.

Preparer discount. Staking by a Preparer is optional. A Preparer that stakes 50,000 AUDT receives a 20 percent discount on preparation costs. Each additional 50,000 AUDT staked adds 10 percent to the discount, up to a maximum discount of 50 percent. The stake of a PVN does not count toward the discount. AUDT staked for the discount is locked for two years and is then released on the same terms as the stake of a PVN.

Preparation. Preparation costs are the prices that we charge a Preparer for preparing disclosures in LucaSuite™. Every Preparer pays them, whether or not it operates a PVN. We set those prices and publish them.

Transfers of AUDT. Transfers of AUDT are locked until the day named in the Form TR Signal. Until that day, AUDT can move only to and from the Smart Contracts: on delivery, on staking and unstaking, in payment for a validation, as a reward, as a penalty and on a daily release. It cannot be transferred from one wallet to another. A sale of a Unit after two years is not affected, because the stake moves within the validator staking contract. One movement between persons is possible while the lock applies: a User that engages a cohort of PVNs pays the Operators that it has chosen. When we give the Form TR Signal, we name the day on which we intend AUDT to be listed for trading, and the lock ends on that day. That day cannot be earlier than the day on which the Form TR Signal takes effect or more than 14 days after it. It cannot be changed once the Form TR Signal has taken effect, and the lock ends on it whether or not any venue has listed AUDT.
xbrli:xbrl.regca:FunctionalAssetDescription:

xbrli:xbrl.regca:ConflictsOfInterestAndRelatedPerso:
The Auditchain License. Auditchain has granted us a global and exclusive license to Pacioli and the Disclosure Models, with the right to sublicense. Mr. Meyers, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, is Lead Architect of Auditchain and controls both Auditchain and us. The first is 28,250,000 AUDT, which is 50 percent of the treasury allocation and is deliverable to Auditchain after the filing of Form TR. The second is a royalty of 20 percent of the revenue that we derive, in whatever form we receive it, excluding the proceeds of our offerings. No cash is payable for the AUDT component. Auditchain is our related person because it is an affiliate under common control with us. Auditchain remains our licensor after the filing of Form TR. Under each Node License, an Operator may run in production any version of the PVN software that passes Conformance Validation, whoever changed the code, and neither we nor Auditchain can withdraw that right.

The Initial Key Holders. Mr. Meyers signs for us as one of the five Initial Key Holders. The other four are Operators of Founding PVNs that are not affiliated with us. Until the Handover, the Key Holder Contract holds our keys to the Smart Contracts, and it cannot act without our signature, as described under "Smart contract governance mechanisms."

The Governance Council and the Guardian. Neither we nor Auditchain may hold a seat on the Governance Council, and neither may any of our or its affiliates, founders, directors, officers, employees or advisers. Mr. Meyers holds no seat. The Guardian is the Council Contract. We are never the Guardian.

Our PVN. We operate one PVN, staked with 50,000 AUDT from the treasury allocation, and may earn validation rewards as an Operator. Like every other PVN, it receives a share of the AUDT Subsidies; by August 31, 2027, it had received 3,226 AUDT. PVNs that we operate are not counted toward the 30 PVNs of our second promised essential managerial effort. Our PVN has no vote in the election of the Operator members of the Governance Council.

Minting. Until the Handover, the Key Holder Contract mints the AUDT delivered in our offerings and the other allocations, up to 136,083,333 AUDT in total, on the signatures described under "Smart contract governance mechanisms." The liquidity allocation is 20,000,000 AUDT and the treasury allocation is 56,500,000 AUDT. Before the Handover, we will mint 12,000,000 AUDT of the liquidity allocation into the three liquidity contracts, which we cannot withdraw from, and the other 8,000,000 AUDT and the treasury allocation in full to ourselves. The right of the Key Holder Contract to mint AUDT ends at the Handover. After it, AUDT can be minted only by the Subsidies Contract, the Claims Contract and the Council Contract, each up to a cap written in its code, as described under "Supply." After we deliver 28,250,000 AUDT to Auditchain, we will retain 36,250,000 AUDT (12.08 percent of the maximum supply), of which 8,000,000 AUDT is for centralized exchanges, and Auditchain will hold 28,250,000 AUDT (9.42 percent). No lockup applies to the AUDT held by either of us, other than the lock on transfers of all AUDT described under "Lockups" and the two-year lock on the 50,000 AUDT staked for our PVN.

Settings and fees. Until the Governance Contract is deployed, we alone set the allocation of rewards, which includes the rate of AUDT Subsidies and the division of each validation fee among its recipients. Until the Handover, we alone set the other settings of the Smart Contracts, including the stake of a PVN. We can change each of them at any time until then, and a change can raise or lower what an Operator earns.

Voting power. No more than 137,083,333 AUDT will be outstanding when we file Form TR. We will then hold at least 47.1 percent of the AUDT outstanding. That share counts the 8,000,000 AUDT for centralized exchanges and does not count the 12,000,000 AUDT in the liquidity contracts, which we do not control and which carries no vote. Governance Votes open when the Form TR Signal takes effect. From then, we and Auditchain may delegate and vote the AUDT that we hold like any other holder. As for every holder, AUDT that either of us holds on a centralized exchange must first be withdrawn to a wallet that we control and delegated. If we delegate and vote our 64,500,000 AUDT, we can defeat any proposal put to a Governance Vote and carry any settings proposal, and we can carry any general proposal unless more than 32,250,000 votes are cast against it. While the 8,000,000 AUDT is on centralized exchanges, we can cast 56,500,000 votes, and other holders could carry or defeat a settings proposal if they cast more votes than we do. We cannot block a mint from the reserve, which needs no Governance Vote. We cannot carry out any proposal without the approval of the Governance Council. After we deliver 28,250,000 AUDT to Auditchain, the same is true of us and Auditchain together. The risk factors describe this further.

Payments and royalties. We are not a party to direct payments between Users and Operators. We receive no part of those payments, except that the PVN that we operate may earn a share of them on the same terms as every other PVN. We pay Auditchain the royalty of 20 percent of our revenue described above, which excludes the proceeds of our offerings. The royalty accrues on our staking rewards, on any validation rewards that our PVN earns, including rewards paid in AUDT, and on the preparation costs that Preparers pay us. The royalty on AUDT Subsidies and other rewards paid to our PVN in AUDT is paid in AUDT, after the day named in the Form TR Signal. The royalty also accrues on the trading fees that the liquidity contracts pay us.

Auditchain's activities. Auditchain receives no taxonomy-developer rewards for the Disclosure Models that it developed. Auditchain operates its own validator on Ethereum and intends to operate its own validator on Polygon PoS and its own full node on Robinhood Chain, as we do. It earns staking rewards on the same basis as any other participant in those networks (see the sections on issuer and affiliate blockchain network participation). Auditchain does not operate a PVN. Auditchain is the developer of the Reg CA Disclosure Model, which is the first reporting scheme. Only the person that filed a reporting scheme, or the regulator or standard setter whose requirement it carries, can file a change to it. Neither we nor Auditchain, nor any person that is excluded from the Governance Council because of its connection with either of us, may act as the delegate of an MCV.

The MCVs. The MCVs receive one half of every penalty that is taken from the stake of a PVN. That includes the penalty for a PVN that does not undergo its annual Conformance Validation, which the MCVs or their delegates perform, so that an MCV could gain from its own delay. For that reason, a PVN is not penalized if its Operator requested the Conformance Validation and paid the Conformance Fee at least 30 days before it was due and the MCVs performed it late. The MCVs will also hold seats on the Governance Council. Each of the two initial MCVs received its stake of 250,000 AUDT from us without cost, for establishing the Network. After the filing of Form TR, we may give a later MCV its stake out of our treasury allocation.

Our activities after the filing of Form TR. After the Handover, we will keep two rights in the Smart Contracts: the right to name the recipients of the team and advisor allocations, and the Form TR Signal. Outside the Smart Contracts, we will continue to hold the Auditchain License, to charge preparation costs and to issue vLEIs, and Auditchain will remain our licensor. After the filing of Form TR, we may develop taxonomies and data-analytics tools and participate in the Network on the same basis as any other third party, with four exceptions. We may not hold a seat on the Governance Council. Our PVN has no vote in the election of its Operator members. We cannot be paid consultation rewards. We may not act as the delegate of an MCV. As a developer of taxonomies, we may then earn royalties on the same basis as any other developer.

xbrli:xbrl.regca:AssociatedCryptoApplicationMateria:
Pacioli is designed as a decentralized protocol for preparing and validating regulatory disclosures. It has two functions.

Preparation. Preparers prepare machine-readable disclosures in Pacioli from disclosure models published by standard setters and regulators.

Validation. Independent PVNs check each disclosure against the Technical Specifications that apply to the reporting scheme under which it was prepared. Those specifications are the XBRL 2.1 and XBRL Formula specifications, the Open Information Model and xBRL-JSON (Project Tavi), the Reg CA Disclosure Model, and all other disclosure models based on the XBRL specifications.

Two kinds of nodes operate on the Network.

(1) MCVs. Two standard setters serve as the initial MCVs. Other global standard setters that specify data and taxonomy formats may also serve as MCVs. The two initial MCVs are named in the Smart Contracts at their deployment. No person holds a right to admit or remove an MCV before Governance Votes open. After that, an MCV is admitted or removed only by a Governance Vote together with the approval of the Governance Council. Each MCV must name at least one qualified delegate to perform its Conformance Validations on time, and the MCV decides who is qualified. Neither we nor Auditchain, nor any person that is excluded from the Governance Council because of its connection with either of us, may act as a delegate. The MCVs verify that each PVN conforms to the Technical Specifications. A PVN is admitted to the Network only after it passes a Conformance Validation, and it must undergo a Conformance Validation each year. Each MCV operates a node and stakes 250,000 AUDT. We allocated 250,000 AUDT to each of the two initial MCVs outside our offerings, without cost, for establishing the Network. That allocation counts toward the $5,000,000 limit of the startup exemption. After the filing of Form TR, we may give a later MCV its stake out of our treasury allocation. We have not promised to do so. The MCVs earn the fees that Operators pay for Conformance Validations, a share of each validation fee and one half of the penalties taken from the stakes of PVNs. The MCVs pay no fees.

(2) PVNs. PVNs validate and analyze the regulatory disclosures that issuers of crypto assets prepare under Reg CA and under other reporting schemes. The Agent is part of the PVN software on every PVN. It uses an algorithm that is designed to search for, detect and fulfill requests for the validation or analysis of machine-readable crypto asset white papers and financial statements. Each PVN continuously scans the Network for such requests. When a request is detected, the Agent initiates a race among the PVNs to fulfill it. The Agent also governs how the other PVNs reach consensus with the PVN that wins the race. The Agent allocates the rewards to the winning PVN and to the other PVNs that reach consensus with, and corroborate, the winning PVN. The share of a validation fee for the corroborating PVNs is divided equally among them.

The software that we license with each PVN is the means by which Operators participate in Pacioli. An Operator that purchases a Unit without the Node License under the first exception participates through its own software, which must comply with the Technical Specifications and must perform the functions of the Agent.
xbrli:xbrl.regca:PlanOfDevelopment:
We deployed the Subsidies Contract on July 1, 2027, with the Token Contract, the Validation Contract and the Claims Contract. The Subsidies Contract pays AUDT Subsidies in order to accelerate the adoption of Pacioli.

We will report the final transition on Form TR upon the occurrence of three events: the final deployment of the Subsidies Contract, the adoption of a minimum of 30 PVNs, and the deployment of the Governance Contract with the counsel of the Founding PVNs, together with the other steps of our sixth promised effort, which ends with the Handover. The first two of those events have occurred. A sample model of Form TR is provided to the staff of the Commission for demonstration purposes.

The Startup Offering also funded three other efforts. The first is the onboarding of two standard setters as the initial MCVs. The second is the deployment of the Reg CA Disclosure Model to Pacioli as the first reporting scheme. The third is the Security Audit, which we obtained before we deployed the Smart Contracts and the PVN software.

The Subsidies Contract caps the AUDT Subsidies paid before the filing of Form TR at 1,000,000 AUDT, or $1,000,000 at the equivalent price of $1.00 per AUDT in the Startup Offering. That amount is the capacity remaining under the $5,000,000 limit of the startup exemption after the Startup Offering and the allocation to the MCVs. We set the rate at which the Subsidies Contract pays AUDT Subsidies, and we can raise or lower it until the Governance Contract is deployed. We have set the rate so that the Subsidies Contract pays the 1,000,000 AUDT over the whole period from the deployment of the Smart Contracts on July 1, 2027 until the filing of Form TR. Each month, the Subsidies Contract splits the AUDT Subsidies for that month equally among the active PVNs. A PVN is active in a month if, in that month, it validates or analyzes disclosures as the winning PVN or as a corroborating PVN. A PVN that is not active in a month receives no AUDT Subsidies for that month. The more PVNs are active, the smaller the share of each. By August 31, 2027, the Subsidies Contract had paid 100,000 AUDT of AUDT Subsidies. From the deployment of the Governance Contract, the rate of AUDT Subsidies is subject to governance. No person can change it until Governance Votes open. After that, a change to the rate is a settings proposal: it must be put to a Governance Vote of the holders of AUDT and must also receive the approval of the Governance Council. Our PVN receives AUDT Subsidies on the same terms as every other PVN.

After the filing of Form TR, the Governance Council may also direct the Subsidies Contract to pay consultation rewards to persons that comment on a reporting scheme, as described under "Governance mechanisms." Consultation rewards cannot exceed 4,500,000 AUDT in total, and the Governance Council is not obliged to pay any.

We may award rights to claim AUDT from the team and advisor allocations at any time, because the Token Contract, the Subsidies Contract and the Claims Contract are deployed. No AUDT can be claimed under such a right until after the filing of Form TR.

We and our affiliate Auditchain each operate one validator on Ethereum and intend to operate one validator on Polygon PoS and a full node on Robinhood Chain (see the sections on issuer and affiliate blockchain network participation). The purpose is for the Underlying Networks to be secured in part by the participants in Pacioli.

Liquidity. Of the net proceeds of the Tier 2 AUDT Offering, we will use $30,000,000 of USDC, with the 20,000,000 AUDT of the liquidity allocation, to provide liquidity at $1.50 per AUDT when transfers of AUDT open. Before the Handover, we will deploy three liquidity contracts, one on each Underlying Network, mint 12,000,000 AUDT into them (6,000,000 AUDT on Ethereum and, through the bridge, 4,000,000 AUDT on Robinhood Chain and 2,000,000 AUDT on Polygon PoS) and send them $18,000,000 of USDC in the same proportions. On the day on which transfers of AUDT open, any person may call each liquidity contract to deposit its AUDT and USDC in a Uniswap AUDT/USDC pool on its network. The contract then holds the pool position permanently: no one, including us, can withdraw it. It pays us the trading fees that the position earns, which are revenue on which we pay Auditchain its royalty. We will place the other 8,000,000 AUDT and $12,000,000 of USDC with Coinbase (3,000,000 AUDT and $4,500,000), Kraken (2,500,000 AUDT and $3,750,000) and OKX (2,500,000 AUDT and $3,750,000) if they list AUDT. We will provide no liquidity on Robinhood, which is a broker trading application; its customers can reach the pool on Robinhood Chain. This is our intention, not a promise of essential managerial efforts.

This Offering is expansion capital to accelerate the adoption of Pacioli. It adds no promise of essential managerial efforts to the six that are set out in the table of essential managerial efforts. The Network operates with the Founding PVNs under Conformance Validation. At this stage, however, the Network still depends on the cooperation of the MCVs and the Founding PVNs. Our managerial efforts therefore continue through this Offering.

We will use the net proceeds as described under "Intended use of proceeds" to accelerate adoption toward a Network of 740 PVNs. We believe that a Network of that size is sufficient to handle the filing obligations of the world's issuers across the reporting schemes that the Network validates.

Our one remaining promised effort is the sixth effort in the table of essential managerial efforts: to deploy the Governance Contract, the Council Contract, the Scheme Registry and the Consultation Stake Contract with the counsel of the Founding PVNs and after a second audit, to seat the first Governance Council and to carry out the Handover. After the Handover, the code and the settings of the Smart Contracts can be changed only by a Governance Vote together with the approval of the Governance Council. We intend to file Form TR immediately after the Handover.

The Key Holder Contract mints the AUDT that we deliver in our offerings, and its right to mint ends at the Handover. We therefore intend to carry out the Handover only after this Offering and the Tier 2 AUDT Offering have ended. Our target date for the Handover and for the filing of Form TR is December 31, 2028. It is a target, and we do not promise it.

As the issuer of the Units described under "Material terms of the covered investment contract" (regca:CoveredInvestmentContractMaterialTerms), we have structured this Offering in a form that issuers and users of crypto assets already know. That form is a validator node that is activated by a stake of the network's token, earns rewards for work that the network can verify and is slashed for work that it fails to do. The Units carry the same kinds of incentives as the production versions of other decentralized protocols, applied to regulatory disclosure. Those incentives are staking, validation rewards, royalties, slashing and governance.

We believe that compliance with Reg CA will be adopted faster if the disclosures that it requires are prepared and validated through a protocol whose economics are familiar to the people who must comply. This Offering is intended to accelerate the adoption of the Reg CA exemptions and of Pacioli.
xbrli:xbrl.regca:SecurityMaterialAspects:
We license Pacioli from Auditchain. The Smart Contracts are open source. The PVN software, which includes the Agent, is not open source. Its source code is public under the Business Source License 1.1. That license permits a person to copy and modify the code and to use it other than in production. It does not by itself permit production use, and each version becomes available under an open-source license no later than the fourth anniversary of its first public distribution. The Node License permits each Operator to run the PVN software in production. The source code of LucaSuite™ and of the Pacioli Explorer is not public. The source code of the Smart Contracts and of the PVN software is public at https://github.com/Auditchain/. The terms of the Business Source License 1.1 that apply to each version of the PVN software are stated with the published code.

Ironvault Security Labs completed the Security Audit on June 15, 2027, before the Smart Contracts were deployed on July 1, 2027. The Security Audit found no critical or high-severity issues. The report on the Security Audit is published at https://pacioli.ai/security.

A second audit will cover the Governance Contract, the Council Contract, the Scheme Registry, the Consultation Stake Contract and every change that they require in the Smart Contracts already audited. We will obtain it before we deploy those four contracts.

No SOC or ISAE attestation covers the Network. Vendors that build on the Network are responsible for their own attestations. Whether a decentralized network can obtain such an attestation will remain unsettled until the audit standards become clear.

The MCVs test the conformance of each PVN to the Technical Specifications before the PVN is admitted to the Network and each year after that.

(2) the Tier 2 Node Offering: 33,500,000 AUDT (11.17%; 670 Units);

(3) the Tier 2 AUDT Offering: 22,083,333 AUDT (7.36%);

(4) AUDT Subsidies: 45,000,000 AUDT (15.00%), which is the most that the Subsidies Contract can mint and of which no more than 1,000,000 AUDT is paid before the filing of Form TR;

(5) MCV stakes: 500,000 AUDT (0.17%; 250,000 AUDT for each of the two initial MCVs);

(6) team: 30,000,000 AUDT (10.00%);

(7) advisors: 30,000,000 AUDT (10.00%);

(8) partnerships: 30,000,000 AUDT (10.00%), which is part of the Governance Council allocation;

(9) liquidity: 20,000,000 AUDT (6.67%), of which 12,000,000 AUDT (4.00%) will be committed permanently to three liquidity pools and 8,000,000 AUDT (2.67%) is for centralized exchanges;

(10) treasury: 56,500,000 AUDT (18.83%), of which 28,250,000 AUDT (9.42%) is the consideration payable to Auditchain for the Auditchain License and is deliverable after the filing of Form TR, and 28,250,000 AUDT (9.42%) is retained by us; and

(11) reserve: 28,916,667 AUDT (9.64%), which is not minted, is part of the Governance Council allocation and is held for the growth of the Network.

The Token Contract enforces the maximum supply of 300,000,000 AUDT in its code. No AUDT can be minted beyond it, and no upgrade of the Smart Contracts can change it. Each allocation can be minted only by the contract named for it, up to a cap written in the code, and no contract can mint from the cap of another or from what another leaves unminted. The caps add up to the maximum supply: the Key Holder Contract, until the Handover, 136,083,333 AUDT for our offerings, the MCV stakes and the liquidity and treasury allocations; the Subsidies Contract, 45,000,000 AUDT for AUDT Subsidies; the Claims Contract, after the filing of Form TR, 30,000,000 AUDT for each of the team and advisor allocations; and the Council Contract, after the Handover, 58,916,667 AUDT for the Governance Council allocation, which consists of the partnership allocation and the reserve. AUDT that a contract does not mint stays unminted. No other contract can mint it, and no proposal can move it.

After the Handover, the Council Contract can mint from the reserve on the two-thirds approval of the Governance Council, with no Governance Vote. It can mint from the partnership allocation only after a general proposal to mint a stated portion passes a Governance Vote and receives the two-thirds approval of the Governance Council (see "Governance mechanisms"). Each mint names the amount, the purpose and the contract that receives the AUDT. The Governance Council may deploy contracts for bounties, incentives and other purposes, and such a contract receives AUDT only through the Council Contract, within its cap. No AUDT from the Governance Council allocation may be minted to a member of the Governance Council, to its organization or to an affiliate of either, to us or to Auditchain.

AUDT is minted only on Ethereum. On Polygon PoS and Robinhood Chain, bridged AUDT is created only when the same amount of AUDT is locked on Ethereum, and is removed when it returns. The AUDT on the three networks together therefore never exceeds the AUDT minted on Ethereum.

No lockup or release schedule applies to the 8,000,000 AUDT of the liquidity allocation for centralized exchanges or to either part of the treasury allocation, with two exceptions: the 50,000 AUDT staked for our PVN is locked for two years like every other stake, and all AUDT is subject to the lock on transfers that is described under "Lockups." xbrli:xbrl.regca:LockupsDescription:
Units. The 50,000 AUDT delivered with each PVN is staked and locked for a minimum of two years from delivery. If the Operator unstakes, the PVN is deactivated immediately and the Node License ends. A purchaser may sell a Unit after two years if a new Conformance Validation of the PVN is completed before the sale settles and the buyer is an Accredited Investor that holds an LEI or a vLEI. The two-year lock then restarts for the buyer. A Unit purchased without the Node License under the first exception may be resold only as described under "Material terms of the covered investment contract." AUDT that an Operator stakes in addition to the stake of its PVN, to restore that stake or for the Preparer discount, is locked for two years on the same terms.

Tier 2 AUDT Offering. Of the AUDT to be sold in the Tier 2 AUDT Offering, 20 percent will be released at delivery and 80 percent will be released through the release contract in equal daily amounts over one year.

Transfers of AUDT. Transfers of AUDT are locked until the day named in the Form TR Signal. Until that day, AUDT can move only to and from the Smart Contracts: on delivery, on staking and unstaking, in payment for a validation, as a reward, as a penalty and on a daily release. It cannot be transferred from one wallet to another. AUDT can also move to the bridge, to create the bridged AUDT that the liquidity contracts on Polygon PoS and Robinhood Chain hold. A sale of a Unit after two years is not affected, because the stake moves within the validator staking contract. One movement between persons is possible while the lock applies: a User that engages a cohort of PVNs pays the Operators that it has chosen. When we give the Form TR Signal, we name the day on which we intend AUDT to be listed for trading, and the lock ends on that day. That day cannot be earlier than the day on which the Form TR Signal takes effect or more than 14 days after it. It cannot be changed once the Form TR Signal has taken effect, and the lock ends on it whether or not any venue has listed AUDT.

Team and advisor allocations. We may award rights to claim AUDT from the team and advisor allocations at any time, because the Token Contract, the Subsidies Contract and the Claims Contract are deployed. No AUDT can be claimed under such a right until after the filing of Form TR. We have not awarded any right to claim AUDT from the team or advisor allocations. The rights are recorded in the Claims Contract, which releases the AUDT of each award to its holder in equal daily amounts over two years and mints it as it is released. The two years begin on the day on which we give the Form TR Signal, which is the day on which we file Form TR, or, for an award made after that day, on the day of the award. The release continues if the holder ceases to serve us. We will award no right to ourselves, to Auditchain or to any entity that controls, is controlled by or is under common control with either of us. Individuals, including our officers and directors, may receive awards, which we disclose. We will award no right to a member of the Governance Council or to an affiliate of a member while the member sits, or within one year before or after.

Governance Council allocation. The partnership allocation and the reserve form the Governance Council allocation. No AUDT of it is minted before the Handover. AUDT minted from it after the Handover is subject to no lockup, other than the lock on transfers of all AUDT until the day named in the Form TR Signal.

Minting. The right of the Key Holder Contract to mint AUDT ends at the Handover. After the Handover, AUDT can be minted only by the Subsidies Contract, the Claims Contract and the Council Contract, each up to a cap written in its code, as described under "Supply." No contract can mint from the cap of another, and no person can create a further right to mint.

Liquidity and treasury allocations. The 12,000,000 AUDT of the liquidity allocation that is minted into the three liquidity contracts is locked in them permanently, with the USDC paired with it. No lockup applies to the 8,000,000 AUDT of the liquidity allocation for centralized exchanges or to the treasury allocation, other than the lock on transfers described above and the two-year lock on the 50,000 AUDT staked for our PVN. That includes the 28,250,000 AUDT of the treasury allocation that is payable to Auditchain as consideration for the Auditchain License.
xbrli:xbrl.regca:DistributionMethodsDescription:
Operators earn AUDT for validating machine-readable regulatory disclosures. AUDT is distributed in connection with that work in three ways.

(1) Direct payments. A User that requests validation pays the PVNs in AUDT, through the Smart Contracts, and/or in other digital assets that the PVNs accept as payment. There can be no assurance that AUDT will be accepted by PVNs. We are not a party to these payments, and we do not offer or sell anything in connection with them. We receive no part of them, except as described below for the PVN that we operate. Before the Tier 2 AUDT Offering, we sell AUDT only in Units. Until that offering opens, a User that does not operate a PVN cannot obtain AUDT, and a validation can be paid for in AUDT only by a person that has received AUDT as AUDT Subsidies or as a reward, such as an Operator or an MCV.

(2) Royalties. Royalties may be paid to developers of regulatory disclosure taxonomies. When a User requests validation of a disclosure that was prepared with a taxonomy developed by a third party, the User's payment is divided between the taxonomy developer and the other recipients described below. The third party may be a standard setter. A regulator that files its own model takes no royalty. At the date of this document, neither we nor Auditchain receives such a royalty.

(3) AUDT Subsidies. AUDT Subsidies are described under "Plan of development."

Division of each validation fee. Each validation fee is divided among eight groups of recipients, which the table of network reward allocation names for a request put to the whole Network and for a request put to a cohort: the winning PVN, the corroborating PVNs, taxonomy developers, future subsidy replenishment, liquidity, governance staking, airdrops and grants, and the MCVs. The share of the corroborating PVNs is divided equally among the PVNs that corroborate the winning PVN on that request. The table states the percentages in force at the date of this document. The share of taxonomy developers is 10 percent in both cases. We set the division until the Governance Contract is deployed and can change it at any time until then. From that deployment, it is subject to governance, as described under "Governance of the network reward allocation." The division in force is a setting of the Smart Contracts and can be read from the blockchain. It also provides how the share of a taxonomy developer that takes no reward is divided among the other recipients.

The shares for liquidity, governance staking, and airdrops and grants are held in the Smart Contracts. Nothing is paid out of them before the filing of Form TR. After that filing, their use is decided by a Governance Vote together with the approval of the Governance Council. The share for future subsidy replenishment is held by the slash contract and is paid out as AUDT Subsidies after the Form TR Signal has taken effect.

The MCVs receive the fees that Operators pay for Conformance Validations, their share of each validation fee and one half of the penalties taken from the stakes of PVNs.

The PVN that we operate competes for the shares of the winning PVN and of the corroborating PVNs on the same terms as every other PVN. We may therefore be among the recipients of those shares.

In the Node Offerings, we distribute AUDT only as part of Units, with 50,000 AUDT in each Unit. In the Tier 2 AUDT Offering, we intend to distribute AUDT alone, and one unit of the CIC will be one AUDT. The stakes of the two initial MCVs, which are 250,000 AUDT each, were allocated outside our offerings and without cost, for establishing the Network.
xbrli:xbrl.regca:HoldingsByRelatedPersonsDescriptio:
Related persons hold no AUDT. We have not awarded any right to claim AUDT from the team allocation (30,000,000 AUDT) or the advisor allocation (30,000,000 AUDT).

We may award such rights at any time, because the Token Contract, the Subsidies Contract and the Claims Contract are deployed, and no AUDT can be claimed under them until after the filing of Form TR. Upon the filing of Form TR, we intend to award rights to claim 7,500,000 AUDT to Jason Meyers and 1,500,000 AUDT to Thomas Egan, CPA, from the team allocation, and 600,000 AUDT to Avery Lindqvist from the advisor allocation. The Claims Contract releases the AUDT of each award in equal daily amounts over two years. The release of claimed AUDT is described under "Lockups."

No related person has purchased a Unit.

We operate one PVN, staked with 50,000 AUDT from the treasury allocation. Like every other PVN, it receives a share of the AUDT Subsidies, which had reached 3,226 AUDT by August 31, 2027. We owe Auditchain 20 percent of those AUDT as royalty, which we will deliver in AUDT after the day named in the Form TR Signal.
