Of that total, 28,250,000 AUDT is deliverable after the filing of Form TR to Auditchain, a related person and the licensor of Pacioli, as consideration for the Auditchain License, and 8,000,000 AUDT is for our liquidity on centralized exchanges. Auditchain holds no AUDT at the date of this document.
xbrli:xbrl.regca:ReleaseSchedulesDescription:
PVN stakes. When an Operator unstakes, the release contract releases the stake in equal daily amounts over two years.

MCV stakes. The stake of an MCV remains staked for as long as the MCV serves. When an MCV unstakes, the release contract releases the stake in equal daily amounts over two years.

Tier 2 AUDT Offering. Of the AUDT to be sold in the Tier 2 AUDT Offering, 20 percent will be released at delivery and 80 percent will be released in equal daily amounts over one year.

Team and advisor allocations. Claims are made through the Claims Contract after the filing of Form TR. The Claims Contract releases the AUDT of each award in equal daily amounts over two years and mints it as it is released. The release of claimed AUDT is described under "Lockups."

AUDT Subsidies. AUDT Subsidies are paid through the Subsidies Contract, which mints them as they are paid, up to 45,000,000 AUDT. The Subsidies Contract caps the amount paid before the filing of Form TR at 1,000,000 AUDT. After the Form TR Signal has taken effect, AUDT Subsidies are paid first out of the AUDT that the slash contract holds, and the Subsidies Contract mints only the remainder. Our PVN receives AUDT Subsidies on the same terms as every other PVN.

Liquidity and treasury allocations. Before the Handover, we will mint 12,000,000 AUDT of the liquidity allocation into the three liquidity contracts, where it is locked permanently, and the other 8,000,000 AUDT and the remainder of the treasury allocation to ourselves. No release schedule applies to the AUDT minted to us, including the 28,250,000 AUDT of the treasury allocation that is payable to Auditchain for the Auditchain License.

Governance Council allocation. After the Handover, the Council Contract mints AUDT from the partnership allocation and the reserve as described under "Governance mechanisms." No release schedule applies.
xbrli:xbrl.regca:MechanismsForGeneratingAndDestroyi:
AUDT is minted as it is distributed, up to the maximum supply of 300,000,000, which the Token Contract enforces. AUDT is minted only on Ethereum. The mint function of the Token Contract is called in four ways, each up to a cap that is written in the code. No caller can mint from the cap of another, and no upgrade can change a cap or the maximum supply.

(1) Validation rewards. The engagement contract triggers the Validation Contract. The Validation Contract calls the Subsidies Contract, which calls the mint function of the Token Contract. The Subsidies Contract can mint no more than 45,000,000 AUDT. It holds no AUDT: it mints each reward when the reward is paid, so that the AUDT outstanding on the blockchain can be compared at any time with the amounts that we report. After the filing of Form TR, the Governance Council may also direct the Subsidies Contract to pay consultation rewards, within the same cap and within the limits described under "Governance mechanisms."

(2) Offerings and allocations. Until the Handover, the Key Holder Contract calls the mint function for the AUDT delivered in our offerings, the stakes of the two initial MCVs and the stake of our PVN, which is part of the treasury allocation. Before the Handover, it also mints the liquidity allocation, 12,000,000 AUDT of it into the three liquidity contracts and 8,000,000 AUDT to us, and the remainder of the treasury allocation to us. The Key Holder Contract can mint no more than 136,083,333 AUDT, which is the total of those amounts.

(3) Claims. After the filing of Form TR, the Claims Contract calls the mint function when AUDT is released under a right to claim from the team or advisor allocations. It can mint no more than 30,000,000 AUDT for each of those allocations.

(4) The Governance Council allocation. After the Handover, the Council Contract calls the mint function for the partnership allocation and the reserve, as described under "Supply" and "Governance mechanisms." It can mint no more than 58,916,667 AUDT.

The right of the Key Holder Contract to mint ends at the Handover. In the Handover, before its administration key is destroyed, the Key Holder Contract gives the Council Contract its right to mint, capped at 58,916,667 AUDT. After the Handover, the Subsidies Contract, the Claims Contract and the Council Contract are the only ways to mint AUDT, and no person can create another.

The AUDT Subsidies paid before the filing of Form TR are capped at 1,000,000 AUDT. That amount is the capacity remaining under the $5,000,000 limit of the startup exemption after the Startup Offering and the allocation to the MCVs.

The four caps total 300,000,000 AUDT, the maximum supply.

On Polygon PoS and Robinhood Chain, the bridge of each network creates bridged AUDT only when the same amount is locked on Ethereum, and removes it when it returns to Ethereum. This does not change the AUDT outstanding.

No AUDT minted on Ethereum is destroyed. AUDT that is forfeited from a stake is reallocated by the slash contract: 50 percent to AUDT Subsidies and 50 percent to the MCVs.
xbrli:xbrl.regca:MethodsToVerifyTransactionHistory: Transactions in AUDT are recorded on the Underlying Networks on which AUDT is deployed. At the date of this document, those networks are Ethereum and Polygon PoS. Transactions can be verified on the public block explorers of those networks (Etherscan and Polygonscan) at the block-explorer addresses given in the table of the subject crypto asset by network. The address of the Token Contract is the same on Ethereum and Polygon PoS and will be the same on Robinhood Chain.
xbrli:xbrl.regca:GovernanceMechanisms:
Governance Votes open when the Form TR Signal takes effect, which is after the Handover and after we file Form TR. From then, no code and no setting of the Smart Contracts can be changed unless two bodies approve the change: the holders of AUDT, by a Governance Vote, and the Governance Council. Neither can make such a change without the other. This item describes the Governance Vote, the Governance Council, what the Governance Council can do alone, and the rules for reporting schemes, on which nobody votes. Who holds the keys to the Smart Contracts before the Handover is described under "Smart contract governance mechanisms."

Voting power. Voting power comes from AUDT that has been delegated. A holder must first delegate its AUDT, either to itself or to another address, before that AUDT counts for any purpose of governance. Each delegated AUDT carries one vote. AUDT that has not been delegated carries no voting power. AUDT carries a vote when a person holds it in a wallet, or has staked it for a PVN, as an MCV or as a Preparer, and has delegated it. Newly minted AUDT counts like any other AUDT. AUDT that the release contract holds carries no vote until it is released. AUDT that is committed to a liquidity pool carries no vote, and AUDT that is held on a centralized exchange carries a vote only after it is withdrawn to a wallet and delegated.

Proposals. Any address may submit a proposal if, in the block immediately before the submission, it held delegated voting power of more than 1 percent of the AUDT outstanding at that time. In this description, the AUDT outstanding is the total supply of AUDT that has been minted. It is not the maximum supply. An address may have only one proposal pending or open for voting at any one time. A proposal consists of a written description and a list of between one and ten actions. Each action identifies a contract to be called, the function to be called, the data to be supplied and any amount of native currency to be sent with the call.

There are two kinds of proposal. A "settings proposal" changes only one or more of the eight settings listed below, or the division of validation fees, and only within the range that the Smart Contracts fix for each of them. Every other proposal is a "general proposal." A proposal is a general proposal if any of its actions is something other than a change of a setting within its range.

Voting. Voting opens in the block after the proposal is submitted and remains open for 17,280 blocks, which is approximately 2.4 days on Ethereum. While voting is open, any address may vote once on the proposal, either for or against. There is no option to abstain, and a vote cannot be changed or withdrawn once it is cast. A vote may be cast directly or by a signed message that a third party submits on behalf of the voter. The weight of each vote is the voting power delegated to the voter as of the block in which the proposal was submitted. AUDT that is acquired or delegated after that block does not count for that proposal.

Passing. After voting closes, a proposal passes only if (a) the votes in favor exceed the votes against and (b) the votes in favor are at least 4 percent of the AUDT outstanding. A general proposal passes only if, in addition, (c) the votes in favor are at least two-thirds of the votes cast. Conditions (a) and (c) are applied when voting closes. Condition (b) is applied once, when the proposal is placed in the queue, to the AUDT outstanding at that time. A proposal that fails a condition is defeated.

Approval of the Governance Council, queuing and execution. A proposal that has met conditions (a) and (c) can be placed in the queue for execution only if it then meets condition (b) and the Governance Council has approved it, and only within 14 days after voting closes. Otherwise, it lapses. A settings proposal requires the ordinary approval of the Governance Council, and a general proposal requires its two-thirds approval. Both are defined below. The Governance Council may record its approval at any time after the proposal is submitted. It may withdraw its approval, by ordinary approval, until the proposal is queued. Queuing starts a waiting period of two days. After the waiting period, any person may execute the proposal. The timelock, which is part of the Governance Contract and has the same address, then carries out each action of the proposal in order. When a proposal is executed, the Council Contract checks the approvals again, against the number that was required when the proposal was queued. An approval no longer counts only if the member that gave it has since been removed or found to have come under an exclusion, or if it was given with an address that has since been replaced. A sitting member may add its approval until the proposal is executed. A proposal must be executed within 14 days after the waiting period ends. Otherwise, it expires and can no longer be executed.

Cancellation and the Guardian. A proposal may be canceled at any time before it is executed in two cases. First, the Guardian may cancel it. The Guardian is the Council Contract, and it cancels a proposal when the Governance Council so decides by ordinary approval. Second, any person may cancel it if the delegated voting power of the proposer has fallen below 1 percent of the AUDT outstanding. A proposer must therefore keep at least 1 percent for up to approximately 32 days. The Guardian has no other power. No person is the Guardian, and we are never the Guardian.

Scope. A settings proposal can change the following settings, each within the range that the Smart Contracts fix for it. We set the ranges before the Handover. This document does not state them.

(1) the maximum number of PVNs operating on the Network;

(2) the number of AUDT that must be staked to operate a PVN;

(3) the amount of the rewards paid to PVNs through AUDT Subsidies;

(4) the amount of AUDT paid by a User that requests the validation of disclosure instances;

(5) the allocation of the proceeds from data subscriptions between reporting entities and the PVNs in a cohort;

(6) the minimum balance that a Preparer must stake to receive the Preparer discount;

(7) the minimum number of PVNs in a cohort; and

(8) the minimum percentage of the PVNs in a cohort that is required to achieve consensus.

In this list, a "reporting entity" is the issuer whose disclosures are validated, and a "data subscription" is a paid request of a User for an analysis of disclosures. Until transfers of AUDT open, no proposal and no person can set the stake of a PVN above 50,000 AUDT or the maximum number of PVNs below 741.

A general proposal is required for everything else. That includes: any change to the code of a Smart Contract, including the Governance Contract and the Council Contract; a change of a range; a change of the voting rules described in this item, including the two-thirds requirement; a change of the seats, the thresholds or the powers of the Governance Council; a mint of a stated portion of the partnership allocation by the Council Contract; the admission or removal of an MCV; a budget for the Governance Council; a pause or a freeze beyond the limits described below; and a change of the rules for reporting schemes and consultation rewards. No proposal can raise a cap, create a right to mint, move unminted AUDT from one cap to another or mint beyond the maximum supply. The Token Contract enforces each cap and the maximum supply, and no upgrade can change them. A proposal to mint from the partnership allocation names the amount, the purpose and the contract that receives the AUDT.

The Governance Council. The Governance Council has nine voting seats in three groups of three, and observer seats without a vote.

(1) Standard setters. Each MCV holds one seat for as long as it is an MCV. An MCV holds its seat itself and not through a delegate. If there are more than three MCVs, the MCVs choose three among themselves.

(2) Operators. The PVNs elect three Operators. The three seats are elected together, for two years. Each PVN has one vote and votes for one candidate, and the three candidates with the most votes are elected. A recall or a vacancy leads to a new election of all three. The rules for calling an election and for a recall are not yet written. A PVN that is admitted after the filing of Form TR votes only after one year. The first election is held before the Council Contract is deployed. Each vote in it is a message signed with the key of the PVN and is published, so that any person can recount, and the result is written into the Council Contract when it is deployed.

(3) Professional services firms. The members sitting may elect up to three firms, by two-thirds approval and only while at least four members sit. A firm must provide audit, assurance, accounting, legal or regulatory-disclosure services to reporting entities and must hold an LEI. A firm that operates a PVN, or that is an MCV or the delegate of an MCV, cannot take one of these seats. Each of the three seats runs in cycles of three years, whether or not it is filled. The cycles first end one, two and three years after the Governance Council is first seated, so that one seat ends each year. A firm that is elected takes the empty seat with the most time left and serves to the end of that cycle.

Observers. A public authority or a self-regulatory organization that oversees a reporting scheme carried on the Network may take an observer seat at its own request. An observer receives every proposal when it is submitted and may publish a statement on it. It has no vote and no key and receives nothing for the seat.

We expect the first Governance Council to have five members: the two initial MCVs and the three Operators that the PVNs elect. No professional services firm and no regulator has agreed to take a seat.

Who may not sit. None of the following may hold a seat, stand for election or vote in the election of the Operator members: we and Auditchain; any person that controls, is controlled by or is under common control with either of us; the founders, promoters, directors, officers, trustees and employees of either of us; the auditors, counsel, consultants, contractors and other advisers of either of us; the immediate family of any of those persons; and any person that has accepted an award of a right to claim AUDT from the team or advisor allocations. A person is not excluded only because it is an MCV, because it operates a PVN or because we consulted it on the four contracts of our sixth promised effort. One organization, together with its affiliates, holds no more than one seat. Seats are held by organizations, except that an Operator who is an individual holds an Operator seat in his or her own name. Each member that is an organization names the individual who signs for it, and that name is published. The exclusions of this paragraph apply to that individual. So do the bar on awards described under "Lockups" and the bar on consultation rewards described below. Mr. Meyers holds no seat.

How the Governance Council decides. Decisions are counted on the members sitting. A seat that has fallen empty still counts for 90 days, unless a successor has taken it. A member that has recorded nothing for 90 days is not counted until it records something again, and a member can record a vote against a proposal, or a sign of life, as well as an approval. "Ordinary approval" requires more than half of the members counted, from at least two of the three groups. "Two-thirds approval" requires at least two-thirds of the members counted, and it must include at least one standard setter and at least one Operator member for as long as a member of that group sits and may vote on the question. A member does not vote on its own admission or removal, or on whether it has come under an exclusion. With five members counted, ordinary approval requires three members and two-thirds approval requires four. The Governance Council can act only while at least four members from at least two groups sit.

How a seat ends. A seat ends at the end of its term; on resignation; when the PVNs elect anew; when an MCV ceases to be an MCV; when an Operator member has unstaked all of its PVNs; or when two-thirds of the members sitting, the member concerned being counted but not voting, remove a firm or find that a member has come under an exclusion. An Operator member stays until its successor is seated. A seat does not end because a PVN is deactivated. The holders of AUDT alone cannot remove a member. An Operator member or an MCV can replace a lost address with the key of its stake. The address of a firm is replaced by two-thirds approval.

Last resort. If fewer than four members have sat for 90 days, the members still sitting may, by more than half of them, name candidates for the empty firm seats, and the holders of AUDT may confirm them by a Governance Vote in which at least two-thirds of the votes cast are in favor. That Governance Vote requires no approval of the Governance Council and can do nothing else.

What the Governance Council can do alone. Besides approving proposals and canceling them as the Guardian, the Governance Council has five powers that require no Governance Vote. The powers to pause and to freeze pass to it at the Handover.

(1) Pause. By ordinary approval, the Governance Council can pause any Smart Contract other than the Governance Contract and the Council Contract. A pause of the Token Contract, the Scheme Registry or the Consultation Stake Contract requires two-thirds approval. A pause of the Token Contract stops transfers and the minting of AUDT. It does not stop delegation or voting. A pause never stops the voting on a proposal, its approval, its queuing or its execution. All pauses together may last no more than 14 days in any 90 days. A further or longer pause requires a general proposal and lasts no more than 30 days each time. A pause that begins before Governance Votes open lasts until 14 days after they open. The Governance Council can end a pause early.

(2) Freeze. Upon a demand from law enforcement or an order of a court, the Governance Council can, by two-thirds approval, freeze the AUDT at one address or one stake in the validator staking contract. A freeze stops transfers and not votes. It cannot be placed on the address of a Smart Contract. It can be placed on the address of another contract, such as a liquidity pool, only by a general proposal. The Governance Council records the authority, the reference and the date of the demand or order, or a hash of them where publication is forbidden. A freeze ends after 90 days. The Governance Council can renew it once by two-thirds approval and can lift it by ordinary approval when the demand ends. A later renewal, or a new freeze of the same address or stake within one year, requires a general proposal. The Smart Contracts cannot verify that a demand or an order exists. Whether that limit is kept depends on the members.

(3) Its own affairs. The Governance Council elects and removes firm members, seats observers and finds that a member has come under an exclusion.

(4) Reporting schemes and consultation rewards. These powers are described below.

(5) The reserve. By two-thirds approval, the Governance Council can direct the Council Contract to mint AUDT from the reserve, up to 28,916,667 AUDT in total, for bounties, incentives and other purposes that it names, including to contracts that it deploys for those purposes. Each mint names the amount, the purpose and the contract that receives the AUDT, and is recorded on the Network. No AUDT from the Governance Council allocation may be minted to a member, to its organization or to an affiliate of either, to us or to Auditchain. No Governance Vote is taken on a mint from the reserve, and our votes cannot block it.

The Governance Council cannot change code or a setting, move AUDT or admit a PVN. It can mint AUDT only from the reserve and, after a Governance Vote, from the partnership allocation. Apart from those mints, its one power over AUDT is the consultation rewards described below. It cannot fix a defect in a Smart Contract. A fix is a general proposal, which takes at least approximately 4.4 days, and the contract may be paused in the meantime. The Governance Contract and the Council Contract cannot be paused. Every act of the Governance Council is recorded on the Network as structured data. Its seats are unpaid, and it has no budget in the code. The two initial MCVs received their stakes of 250,000 AUDT each from us, without cost, for establishing the Network, and we may give a later MCV its stake. MCVs and Operators earn the fees and rewards that this document describes. Its legal form has not been determined.

Reporting schemes. No Governance Vote and no approval of the Governance Council decides what a reporting scheme says. The "source" of a reporting scheme is the regulator or standard setter that issues the requirement. Its "developer" is the person that files its machine-readable model; a taxonomy developer, as that term is used under "Distribution methods," is a developer. Naming a source says where a requirement comes from. It does not mean that the source has approved the model or takes any part in the Network.

(1) Filing. A new reporting scheme, or a change to one, is filed in the Scheme Registry by its source or its developer, with a statement of what changes and of the rule or publication of the source that it carries. The Scheme Registry accepts a change to a reporting scheme only from the address that filed it, or from an address that its source has proven to be its own. Any other developer may file a rival model of the same requirement.

(2) Comment. Filing opens a consultation period of 60 days. During that period, any person may file public comments, including us and Auditchain. A comment may be a working proposal, such as added elements, sample filings or test results.

(3) Answer. After the 60 days, the filer files the final version with an answer to the comments, which states the comments that it took up, the comments that it did not take up, and why. The final version may differ from the filed one only in ways that those affected could expect from the filing.

(4) Effect. The Scheme Registry checks only the steps: that the 60 days have run, that the answer has been filed and what the scheme tests have reported. A version that has passed the scheme tests takes effect on the date that the filer names. The scheme tests are the published tests in force on the day of filing. The MCVs or their delegates run them against the Technical Specifications, within a deadline that we set before the Handover. No MCV and no delegate tests a reporting scheme that it or its affiliate has filed, or to which it or its affiliate has filed a rival. If no result is reported by the deadline, the version counts as passed. If a failure is reported, the report names the tests that failed and the version is held back for 14 days. It then takes effect unless the Governance Council has refused it. A PVN is not tested again for a new reporting scheme.

(5) Refusal and pause. By two-thirds approval, the Governance Council may refuse a filing, or pause a version for up to 14 days in any 90 days, only for a stated fault of one of three kinds. The first is that the version fails the scheme tests. The second is that it is not what it says it is, because it is not what its source published or because its filer is neither its source nor its developer. The third is that it did not go through the steps above. While a version is paused, the earlier version applies. The Governance Council cannot change what a reporting scheme says. The Smart Contracts cannot verify the stated fault. A member does not vote on a reporting scheme that it or its affiliate has filed, or to which it or its affiliate has filed a rival. That member is still counted, so that its exclusion never makes a refusal easier.

(6) Core and proposals. What the source requires is the core of a reporting scheme, and only the core can cause a disclosure to fail validation. An addition by a contributor is carried as a labeled proposal. A labeled proposal is optional and is never a reason for a disclosure to fail. It becomes part of the core only if the source adopts it.

(7) The process of the source. Where the source has adopted a requirement after its own public process, the consultation on the Network concerns only whether the model carries that requirement correctly. While the comment period of the source is open, a model may be filed as a draft.

(8) Urgent corrections. A filer may mark a change as an urgent correction of an error that makes valid disclosures fail or lets invalid disclosures pass. It takes effect once it has passed the scheme tests, and the 60 days of comment run afterwards.

The Reg CA Disclosure Model is entered as the first reporting scheme when the Scheme Registry is deployed. Its source is the rule of the Commission. That does not mean that the Commission has approved the model. Its developer is Auditchain, which takes no developer reward.

Consultation rewards. After the Form TR Signal has taken effect, the Governance Council may, by two-thirds approval, direct the Subsidies Contract to pay AUDT to persons that comment on a reporting scheme ("consultation rewards"). The Governance Council is not obliged to do so, and we promise no reward. Consultation rewards are minted within the cap of 45,000,000 AUDT of the Subsidies Contract and reduce what remains for validation rewards. They cannot exceed 4,500,000 AUDT in total unless a general proposal changes that ceiling. Within that ceiling, we write into the code before the Handover a limit for all consultation rewards in total, a limit for one consultation, a limit for any 12 months and the minimum stake of a commenter. We have not yet set those four numbers.

For a consultation, the Governance Council may open a pool within the first 14 days of the 60 days. After the answer of the filer, it confirms the commenters to be paid and their shares. A commenter can be paid only on two conditions. First, it must have locked at least the minimum stake in the Consultation Stake Contract for that consultation, from the day of its comment until the answer is filed, and in any case for at least 30 days. Second, its comment must have been taken up in the final version, as the answer of the filer records or as the Governance Council finds by two-thirds approval. The stake is returned in full. A reward follows the contribution and not the size of the stake.

The following cannot be paid a consultation reward: the members of the Governance Council, their organizations and their affiliates; observers; the filer of the reporting scheme and its affiliates; and we, Auditchain and the persons that are excluded from the Governance Council because of their connection with either of us. No Governance Vote is taken on consultation rewards.
xbrli:xbrl.regca:SmartContractGovernanceMechanisms:
Until the Handover, the Key Holder Contract holds our keys to the Smart Contracts on each Underlying Network. Those keys are: the right to mint AUDT for our offerings and allocations, which is limited to 136,083,333 AUDT; the administration key of the Token Contract, which can give an address a right to mint, within the maximum supply, or to freeze; the rights to pause a Smart Contract and to freeze the AUDT at an address; and, until the Governance Contract is deployed, the right to upgrade the code of the Smart Contracts.

From the deployment of the Smart Contracts on July 1, 2027 until August 31, 2027, we alone acted through the Key Holder Contract, and two of our three directors signed. Since August 31, 2027, when the Founding PVNs had been admitted, the Key Holder Contract has acted on the signatures of the Initial Key Holders. We are one of them, and Jason Meyers signs for us. The others are four Operators of Founding PVNs that are not affiliated with us: Ledgerline Compliance LLC, Fenwick Data Services AG, Orbis Disclosure Ltd and Kestrel Regtech Inc. Three of the five Initial Key Holders must sign, and we must be one of the three. That rule also applies to an upgrade of the code. If our key is lost, two of our three directors can replace it. No Initial Key Holder may sit on the Governance Council. An Initial Key Holder that is elected to it gives up its key before it is seated, and the Key Holder Contract, on the signatures of three of the Initial Key Holders, of which ours must be one, names another Operator of a Founding PVN in its place. The Key Holder Contract freezes AUDT only upon a demand from law enforcement or an order of a court. The limits on pauses and freezes that apply to the Governance Council after the Handover do not apply to the Key Holder Contract. A pause or a freeze that it has placed ends at the Handover.

Until the Governance Contract is deployed, we alone set the allocation of rewards, and until the Handover, we alone set the other settings listed under "Governance mechanisms." Several functions of the Smart Contracts wait for the filing of Form TR: Governance Votes, AUDT Subsidies above 1,000,000 AUDT, claims of team and advisor AUDT, consultation rewards and the end of the lock on transfers of AUDT. Only we know when we file. We will therefore give the Form TR Signal in the Smart Contracts immediately before we file Form TR. Six kinds of privileged role exist or will exist: upgrade, admission, minting, the settings, pause and freeze, and the role of the Guardian. Each is described below, with its holder before and after the Handover.

(1) Upgrade. Until the Governance Contract is deployed, the Key Holder Contract can upgrade the Smart Contracts on the signatures of three of the five Initial Key Holders, of which ours must be one. We are one of the Initial Key Holders, and Jason Meyers signs for us. The other four are Operators of Founding PVNs that are not affiliated with us: Ledgerline Compliance LLC, Fenwick Data Services AG, Orbis Disclosure Ltd and Kestrel Regtech Inc. From the deployment of the Governance Contract, no person can upgrade the Smart Contracts until Governance Votes open. From then, an upgrade requires a general proposal that passes a Governance Vote and receives the two-thirds approval of the Governance Council. No upgrade can raise a cap, create a right to mint AUDT, move unminted AUDT from one cap to another or change the maximum supply.

(2) Admission. The MCVs admit a PVN to the Network after it passes a Conformance Validation. The MCVs also perform the annual Conformance Validations, deactivate a PVN whose deficiencies are not cured within 30 days and confirm that the buyer of a Unit that was purchased without the Node License qualifies. The two initial MCVs are named in the Smart Contracts at their deployment. No person holds a right to admit or remove an MCV before Governance Votes open. After that, an MCV is admitted or removed only by a general proposal.

(3) Minting. The mint function of the Token Contract is called by:

(a) the Subsidies Contract, up to 45,000,000 AUDT, for validation rewards, when the Validation Contract invokes it, and for consultation rewards, when the Governance Council directs it after the filing of Form TR;

(b) the Claims Contract, up to 30,000,000 AUDT for each of the team and advisor allocations, when AUDT is released under a right to claim after the filing of Form TR;

(c) the Key Holder Contract, up to 136,083,333 AUDT, until the Handover, for the AUDT delivered in our offerings, the stakes of the two initial MCVs and the liquidity and treasury allocations, which include the stake of our PVN; and

(d) the Council Contract, up to 58,916,667 AUDT, after the Handover, for the Governance Council allocation.

These four caps add up to the maximum supply of 300,000,000 AUDT, which the Token Contract enforces. Until the Handover, the Key Holder Contract also holds the administration key of the Token Contract, which can give another address a right to mint within the maximum supply. In the Handover, it uses that key once, to give the Council Contract its capped right to mint, and the key is then destroyed. After that, no person can create a right to mint. On Polygon PoS and Robinhood Chain, the bridge of each network creates bridged AUDT only against AUDT locked on Ethereum.

(4) Settings. Until the Governance Contract is deployed, we set the allocation of rewards. Until the Handover, we set the other settings. From the deployment of the Governance Contract until Governance Votes open, no person can change the allocation of rewards, and from the Handover until then, no person can change any other setting. Once Governance Votes open, the allocation of rewards and the other settings are changed by a settings proposal that passes a Governance Vote and receives the ordinary approval of the Governance Council.

(5) Pause and freeze. Until the Handover, the Key Holder Contract can pause a Smart Contract and can freeze the AUDT at an address. The limits that apply to the Governance Council do not apply to it. After the Handover, only the Governance Council can do so, within the limits described under "Governance mechanisms."

(6) Guardian. The Council Contract is the Guardian from the deployment of the Governance Contract. It can cancel a proposal before it is executed, by ordinary approval of the Governance Council, and has no other power.

After the Handover, we keep two rights: the right to name the recipients of the team and advisor allocations, and the Form TR Signal. They are described under "Smart contract governance mechanisms."

xbrli:xbrl.regca:EcosystemTechnologyInfrastructure:
The Pacioli Explorer is the entry point to the Network, and our aim is for it to become the global destination for disclosure and analysis. There can be no assurance that it will. It is built for three kinds of disclosure: the disclosures that issuers make under Reg CA, the monthly reserve reports that payment stablecoin issuers publish under the GENIUS Act, and the crypto-asset white papers that MiCAR requires. The Reg CA Disclosure Model is the first reporting scheme on the Network; the others will appear on the Pacioli Explorer once reporting schemes for them are added to the Network. Anyone can use it to look up an issuer and see each disclosure that the issuer has sent for validation, year by year. A color-coded indicator shows at a glance whether each disclosure is fully compliant, has only non-critical findings, is not compliant or is still being validated, and a corrected disclosure is linked to the one it corrects. For each disclosure, the Pacioli Explorer shows the PVNs that validated it and whether any of them disagreed with the result the others reached. It also links to the blockchain transactions that record the request, each PVN's result and the final consensus. Each PVN and each MCV has its own page. A PVN's page shows whether its Conformance Validation is current, the MCVs that attested it, the work it has done, the issuers and reporting schemes it serves, and its reputation score. An MCV's page shows the PVNs it has tested, how its results compare with those of the other MCVs, and its reliability score. Both scores are calculated only from records on the blockchain, using formulas published on the Pacioli Explorer. A map shows where issuers, PVNs and MCVs are located and how they are connected. A directory lists the providers of disclosure software and services and their status on the Network.

Pacioli is a web3 application based on Ethereum. AUDT is an ERC20-compatible utility token. The Smart Contracts are developed in Solidity and can be deployed to any blockchain based on Ethereum.

Pacioli has two main components. The first is LucaSuite™, the disclosure automation infrastructure in which disclosure models and machine-readable disclosures are created. The second is the PVN software, a logic and reasoning engine that reads and understands disclosures and detects inconsistencies in them.

The Smart Contracts allow a User that creates disclosures to engage the open Network of PVNs or a private cohort. The Pacioli Explorer gives the public access to validated disclosures.

The Pacioli Explorer is designed as a user-friendly, decentralized EDGAR. Each disclosure published on the Pacioli Explorer carries a canonical cryptographic proof, recorded on-chain, that links the issuer, the PVN that validated the disclosure and the disclosure itself. It also carries the proof that the PVN passed its most recent Conformance Validation and, where the statements in the disclosure describe activity on a blockchain network, the proof that ties those statements to that activity. Where the disclosure is filed with the Commission, it also carries the proof of its filing on EDGAR.

Through an application programming interface (API), wallets, trading platforms and other applications can show their users a validated disclosure, its compliance indicator and its proofs. They can also record that a purchaser received the disclosure, as filed, before completing a purchase (a "proof of reliance").

We license Pacioli from Auditchain under the Auditchain License, which is global and exclusive and includes the right to sublicense. The source code of the Smart Contracts and of the PVN software is public at https://github.com/Auditchain/. The Smart Contracts are open source, and the PVN software is public under the Business Source License 1.1, as described under "Material aspects of the security of the subject crypto asset and the network or application."

At June 30, 2027, cash was $1,287,500 and equity was $(340,000). Equity was negative because the deferred Unit revenue is a liability until it is recognized.

Since June 30, 2027, we have sold the remaining 35 Units for $1,750,000 at closings on July 6 and August 27, 2027. We bought 32 ETH for our Ethereum validator for $128,000. We deployed the Smart Contracts on July 1, 2027, after the Security Audit. In July and August 2027, the Subsidies Contract paid 100,000 AUDT of AUDT Subsidies. Cash at August 31, 2027 was approximately $1,754,000, after the operating expenses of July and August 2027.

We plan to spend about $1,550,000 in the third quarter of 2027 and $1,750,000 in the fourth quarter, before offering expenses. We intend to use the net proceeds as described under "Intended use of proceeds." There is no minimum offering amount.

Pacioli Labs, Inc. (the "Company") was formed in Delaware on September 30, 2026. Capitalized terms that are used in these notes and are not defined in them have the meanings given to them under "Current stage of development" in this document.

The Company holds the Auditchain License from Auditchain, an affiliate under common control with the Company (Note 5). Jason Meyers controls both companies. The Auditchain License is perpetual, global and exclusive. It covers Pacioli and the Disclosure Models, includes future versions and gives the Company the right to sublicense.

The Company sells Units of a CIC under Reg CA. Each Unit is a PVN and consists of 50,000 AUDT, delivered staked, with a Node License. A provider of regulatory disclosure management software or services may purchase a Unit without the Node License on the conditions that this document describes.

Pacioli is designed as a decentralized protocol for the preparation and validation of machine-readable regulatory disclosures. The Network went live on August 31, 2027 with the Founding PVNs. The Company also operates one PVN and one validator on the Ethereum network.
xbrli:xbrl.regca:FinancialStatementNoteTitle: Basis of presentation and significant accounting policies
xbrli:xbrl.regca:FinancialStatementNoteText:
The financial statements are prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (U.S. GAAP). The Company's fiscal year ends on December 31. The first fiscal period ran from formation on September 30, 2026 to December 31, 2026.

Use of estimates. The preparation of financial statements requires estimates that affect the reported amounts. The significant estimates are the fair value of AUDT issued for services, the fair value of the crypto assets that the Company holds, and the income tax rate.

Characterization of the Units for accounting purposes. Reg CA treats the Units that the Company sells as securities (CICs) for the purposes of the Securities Act. That characterization governs the Company's disclosure obligations. It does not determine the accounting. The Units are not equity of the Company, because holders have no residual interest in the Company. The Units are not financial liabilities, because the Company has no obligation to deliver cash or other financial assets to holders. The Units are contracts with customers for the delivery of goods and services within the scope of ASC 606. Those goods and services are AUDT, the Node License and participation in an operating Network. The two characterizations do not conflict. The aggregate offering price reported under Reg CA equals the revenue recognized when the Units are delivered. The offering expenses reported under Reg CA are the Placement Agent compensation, which is shown as cost of revenue, and the other offering expenses, which are shown in operating expenses.

Revenue recognition (ASC 606). The Company's revenue recognition policies cover three sources: (a) Units, (b) AUDT sold alone and (c) staking rewards.

(a) Units. The Company applies the five steps of ASC 606 as follows.

Step 1, contract. Each Unit purchase and license agreement, approved by both parties, is a contract with a customer. The promises in the Company's disclosures on Form 1-SU and Form 1-CRYPTO are promises implied by the Company's published statements and form part of the contract (ASC 606-10-25-16).

Step 2, performance obligations. The Company promises (i) 50,000 AUDT delivered staked, (ii) a Node License, unless the Unit is purchased without the Node License (Note 1), and (iii) an operating Network in which the PVN can be admitted and earn rewards. An operating Network means that the Founding PVNs are under Conformance Validation and that the Subsidies Contract and the Reg CA Disclosure Model are deployed. None of these promises is distinct from the others. The staked AUDT cannot be used without PVN software, the PVN software has no use without an operating Network, and the purchaser cannot benefit from any one of them on its own (ASC 606-10-25-19). The nature of the promise is to transfer a combined item (ASC 606-10-25-21). The three promises are therefore combined into a single performance obligation (ASC 606-10-25-22). The deployment of the Governance Contract that is promised in the plan of development is an activity that the Company undertakes for the Network as a whole. It transfers no good or service to a purchaser and is not a performance obligation (ASC 606-10-25-17).

Step 3, transaction price. The transaction price is the fixed Unit price, which is $50,000 in the Startup Offering and $62,500 in the Tier 2 Node Offering. The Company receives the price in USDC or USDT and converts it to U.S. dollars on receipt (ASC 606-10-32-2). The Company pays the compensation of the Placement Agent out of the proceeds. That compensation does not reduce the transaction price.

Step 4, allocation. The entire price is allocated to the single performance obligation.

Step 5, recognition. The performance obligation is satisfied at a point in time (ASC 606-10-25-30). The Node License is a right to use intellectual property, which is satisfied at a point in time (ASC 606-10-55-58B). The point in time is when the purchaser obtains control of a delivered, staked PVN in an operating Network (ASC 606-10-25-23). For Units sold before the Network began operating, that point was August 31, 2027. By that date, the Founding PVNs had been admitted, and on that date the Network went live as the minimally viable Network of the plan of development. For Units sold after that date, that point is delivery at the closing. Consideration received before that point is presented as a contract liability (ASC 606-10-45-2).

Alternative considered and rejected. The Company considered deferring all Unit revenue until it files Form TR, on the view that its remaining plan-of-development promise is part of what purchasers paid for. The Company rejected that view for two reasons. First, once the Network operates, purchasers direct the use of their PVNs and obtain the benefits of their PVNs without further action by the Company. Those benefits are validation work, rewards and staking. Second, the Governance Contract benefits the Network generally and does not transfer a good or service to a purchaser (ASC 606-10-25-17). Control therefore transfers at the launch of the Network and not upon the filing of Form TR.

(b) AUDT sold alone. The Company intends to make the Tier 2 AUDT Offering, in which each unit of the CIC will be one AUDT. Of each purchase, 20 percent will be delivered to the purchaser's wallet at closing and 80 percent will be delivered at closing to a release contract. Those units will carry no PVN, Node License or Network promise. The Company will recognize the revenue when the AUDT is delivered to the purchaser or to the release contract, which acts for the purchaser. The Company had sold no AUDT in the Tier 2 AUDT Offering at the dates of these statements.

(c) Staking rewards. The Company activated its validator on the Ethereum network on August 20, 2027 and receives ETH as rewards for operating it. It will receive POL as rewards for the validator that it intends to operate on the Polygon PoS network. The Company recognizes those rewards as revenue when it receives them, measured at the fair value of the units on that date. That fair value becomes their cost basis. The Company had received no staking rewards at the dates of these statements.

The Company also charges Preparers for preparing disclosures in LucaSuite™, at prices that it publishes. It had no revenue from preparation in the periods presented.

Costs to obtain contracts (ASC 340-40). The Company pays the Placement Agent compensation of 7 percent of gross proceeds at each closing. That compensation is an incremental cost of obtaining a contract (ASC 340-40-25-2). Where the related revenue is deferred, the Company recognizes the compensation as an asset (ASC 340-40-25-1), presents it in other assets and expenses it as cost of revenue when the revenue is recognized (ASC 340-40-35-1). Where the revenue is recognized at the closing, the Company expenses the compensation at the closing. The Company expenses other offering expenses as incurred.

Crypto assets (ASC 350-60). The Company measures crypto assets other than AUDT at fair value at each reporting date. It held none at the dates of these statements. It recognizes changes in fair value in net income and presents them separately from changes in the carrying amount of other intangible assets (ASC 350-60-35-1, 350-60-45-1, 350-60-45-2). The Company determines cost basis by specific identification. It measures rewards received at fair value on receipt (ASC 350-60-50-2). AUDT that the Company mints for its own account is a self-created intangible asset. That AUDT is the stake of the Company's PVN, the AUDT Subsidies paid to that PVN and, before the filing of Form TR, the treasury allocation and the 8,000,000 AUDT of the liquidity allocation for centralized exchanges. The Company does not recognize that AUDT. It discloses it.

AUDT issued for services. The Company delivers AUDT to the MCVs for establishing the Network and pays AUDT Subsidies to Operators for validation work. The Company recognizes that AUDT as an expense as the services are received. It measures the expense at $1.00 per AUDT, which is the equivalent price per AUDT at which it sold Units in the Startup Offering. AUDT that the Subsidies Contract pays to the Company's own PVN is not recognized as an expense or as an asset, because the Company does not recognize its own AUDT. The royalty that the Company owes Auditchain on those AUDT, 20 percent, is payable in AUDT after transfers of AUDT open. The Company recognizes it as royalty expense at $1.00 per AUDT and as an obligation to deliver the subject crypto asset. The Company uses the same amount to count these issuances toward the $5,000,000 limit of the startup exemption. Where a mixture of cash and non-cash consideration is to be received, Rule 100 of Reg CA bases the aggregate offering price on the price at which the CIC is offered for cash. The Company credits contributed capital, by analogy to equity-classified awards under ASC 718 (ASC 718-10-25-2). That treatment rests on three facts. The AUDT delivered imposes no obligation on the Company to transfer cash or other financial assets. The recipients perform services for the Network. No asset is derecognized, because self-created AUDT is not recognized. The Company considered recognizing a contract liability and rejected that alternative, because the Company has no remaining performance obligation to the recipients once the Network operates. These issuances are noncash transactions. They are excluded from the statement of cash flows and are disclosed in these notes (ASC 230-10-50-4).

Transactions with entities under common control. The Company records assets acquired from an entity under common control with the Company at their carrying amounts in the accounts of the transferring entity at the date of transfer, and not at fair value. The Company records the obligation incurred as consideration at the same amount and recognizes no gain or loss. An agreement that is not yet effective is not recognized but is disclosed (Note 5).

Obligation to deliver AUDT. An obligation to deliver units of AUDT that the Company has not yet minted is a liability until the units are delivered and the Company is relieved of the obligation (ASC 405-20-40-1). The Company recognized no such liability at the dates of these statements (Note 5).

Income taxes (ASC 740). Income tax expense is the current tax on taxable income at an estimated combined federal and state rate of 27 percent. The Company uses that rate as a placeholder until its state apportionment is determined. The 2026 operating loss gave rise to a deferred tax asset. The Company recorded a full valuation allowance against that asset at December 31, 2026, because it was not more likely than not that a startup with no revenue would realize it. The Company expects to use the loss in 2027. No other temporary differences existed at the dates of these statements. The Company therefore recognizes no deferred tax assets or liabilities.

Related persons (ASC 850). Transactions with Auditchain, an affiliate under common control with the Company, are described in Note 5.
The Company received an initial equity capital contribution of $1,000,000 on formation.

Expenses of $10,000 consist of corporate formation expenses of $5,000 and $5,000 for the preparation of the Reg CA disclosure. The Company paid both amounts in cash in the period. The Company had no revenue in the period. At December 31, 2026, the Company had no liabilities and no crypto assets, and its cash was $990,000. The Company recognized no income tax benefit for the operating loss (Note 2).
xbrli:xbrl.regca:FinancialStatementNoteTitle: The Auditchain License; related person transactions
xbrli:xbrl.regca:FinancialStatementNoteText:
On September 30, 2026, the Company entered into the Auditchain License with Auditchain. The Auditchain License is perpetual, global and exclusive. It covers Pacioli and the Disclosure Models, includes future versions and gives the Company the right to sublicense.

Auditchain is a related person of the Company. The two companies are under common control. Jason Meyers, the Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Financial Officer and a director of the Company, controls both companies and is Lead Architect of Auditchain.

The Auditchain License became effective on April 5, 2027, at the first closing of the Startup Offering. Its effectiveness was subject to no other condition.

The consideration for the Auditchain License has two parts. The first is 28,250,000 AUDT, which is 50 percent of the treasury allocation of AUDT and is deliverable to Auditchain after the Company files Form TR. The fair value of that AUDT is $28,250,000 at $1.00 per AUDT, which is the equivalent price per AUDT at which the Company sold Units in the Startup Offering. The second is a royalty of 20 percent of the revenue that the Company derives, in whatever form it is received, excluding the proceeds of the Company's offerings. No cash is payable for the AUDT component.

Because the parties are under common control, the Company recorded the Auditchain License and the obligation to deliver the AUDT at the carrying amount of the software in the accounts of Auditchain on the effective date (Note 2). That carrying amount is nil. The Company therefore recognizes no asset and no liability. It discloses the obligation to deliver 28,250,000 AUDT after the filing of Form TR as a commitment (Note 6).

The royalty applies to revenue other than offering proceeds. It also applies to validation rewards that the Company's PVN earns, including rewards paid in AUDT, and to preparation costs that Preparers pay the Company. The Company had no such revenue at the dates of these statements, and no royalty had accrued. The Company recognizes the royalty as an expense as that revenue is earned and pays it in the following period, except that the royalty on AUDT is paid in AUDT after transfers of AUDT open.

Because the parties are related and under common control, the terms of the Auditchain License are not the result of arm's-length negotiation.

The Company and Auditchain each operate one validator on Ethereum and intend to operate one validator on Polygon PoS and a full node on Robinhood Chain. Auditchain provides no services to the Company other than the Auditchain License, and the Company makes no payment to Auditchain other than the royalty and the delivery of AUDT described above.

Related persons hold no AUDT. The Company intends to award rights to claim AUDT from the team and advisor allocations upon the filing of Form TR. The Claims Contract will release the AUDT of each award in equal daily amounts over two years. The rights are for 7,500,000 AUDT for Jason Meyers, 1,500,000 AUDT for Thomas Egan, CPA, and 600,000 AUDT for Avery Lindqvist. The Company recognizes no expense for them until they are awarded.

Under the Auditchain License described in Note 5, the Company is committed to deliver 28,250,000 AUDT to Auditchain after it files Form TR. The fair value of that AUDT is $28,250,000 at the price of $1.00 per AUDT. The Company is also committed to pay Auditchain 20 percent of its revenue, excluding offering proceeds.

The Company pays Northstar Node Hosting LLC $500 per month for each validator or node that it hosts. That arrangement can be cancelled on 30 days' notice. The Company has no other commitments.

The Company evaluated subsequent events through March 15, 2027, the date of the report of the independent accountant. For the reissuance of these statements in the offering statement, the Company evaluated subsequent events through September 1, 2027.

After December 31, 2026, the following events occurred.

(1) On February 15, 2027, the Company engaged the Placement Agent.

(2) On April 5, 2027, the Company held the first closing of the Startup Offering. The Auditchain License described in Note 5 became effective at that closing. The Company recognized no asset or liability, because the carrying amount is nil.

(3) On April 5, 2027, the Company allocated 500,000 AUDT to the two initial MCVs.

(4) On July 1, 2027, the Company deployed the Smart Contracts, after the Security Audit.

(5) On August 15, 2027, the Company bought 32 ETH for its Ethereum validator for $128,000.

(6) On August 27, 2027, the Company completed the Startup Offering of 70 Units. Gross proceeds were $3,500,000 and net proceeds were $3,225,000.

(7) In July and August 2027, the Subsidies Contract paid 100,000 AUDT of AUDT Subsidies to the PVNs on the Network. The Company recognized the 96,774 AUDT paid to PVNs other than its own as AUDT issued for services of $96,774, which is noncash. The other 3,226 AUDT were paid to the Company's PVN.

(8) By August 31, 2027, the Founding PVNs had been admitted to the Network, and the Network went live on that date. That event satisfied the performance obligation on all 70 Units. The Company recognized revenue of $3,500,000 and cost of revenue of $245,000 on that date.
xbrli:xbrl.regca:FinancialStatementNoteTitle: Basis of presentation of the interim financial statements
xbrli:xbrl.regca:FinancialStatementNoteText:
These unaudited interim financial statements are as of June 30, 2027 and for the six months ended June 30, 2027. They are condensed. They are prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (U.S. GAAP) for interim financial information (ASC 270) and with Rule 8-03(a) of Regulation S-X.

The interim financial statements apply the accounting policies described in Note 2 to the annual financial statements. Those policies include the recognition of Unit revenue under ASC 606 when a delivered, staked PVN is in an operating Network and the treatment of Placement Agent compensation under ASC 340-40.

The independent accountant has not audited or reviewed the interim financial statements. In the opinion of management, all adjustments necessary in order to make the interim financial statements not misleading, consisting only of normal recurring adjustments, have been included.
xbrli:xbrl.regca:FinancialStatementNoteTitle: Results of operations and financial position for the period
xbrli:xbrl.regca:FinancialStatementNoteText:
During the six months ended June 30, 2027, the Company sold 35 of the 70 Units of the Startup Offering at closings on April 5, May 3 and June 1, 2027 for $1,750,000. The Company presented that amount as a contract liability at June 30, 2027, because the Network had not yet begun operating (Note 2 to the annual financial statements, as applied in these interim financial statements). The Placement Agent compensation of $122,500 on those Units is an asset, presented in other assets. The Company will expense it as cost of revenue when the revenue is recognized. The Company recognized no revenue in the period.

Operating expenses were $1,830,000. They consist of marketing of $500,000, development of $400,000, legal and policy of $150,000, general and administrative of $250,000, other offering expenses of $30,000 and $500,000 for 500,000 AUDT allocated to the MCVs at $1.00 per AUDT (AUDT issued for services). That amount is noncash and was credited to contributed capital. The net loss was $1,830,000. The Company recognized no tax benefit, because the realization of the loss depended on the recognition of the deferred Unit revenue, which occurred after the period.

Cash was $1,287,500 at June 30, 2027. That amount reflects the proceeds of the three closings, net of Placement Agent compensation ($1,627,500), less cash operating expenses. Equity was $(340,000) at June 30, 2027, because the deferred Unit revenue is a liability until it is recognized. The deficit reverses on recognition.

The Auditchain License became effective on April 5, 2027, at the first closing. The Company recognized no asset or liability, because the carrying amount is nil.

The Company evaluated subsequent events through September 1, 2027.

After June 30, 2027, the following events occurred.

(1) On July 1, 2027, the Company deployed the Smart Contracts, after the Security Audit.

(2) On July 6, 2027 and August 27, 2027, the Company sold the remaining 35 Units of the Startup Offering for $1,750,000. Placement Agent compensation on those Units was $122,500.

(3) On August 15, 2027, the Company bought 32 ETH for its Ethereum validator for $128,000.

(4) In July and August 2027, the Subsidies Contract paid 100,000 AUDT of AUDT Subsidies to the PVNs on the Network. The Company recognized the 96,774 AUDT paid to PVNs other than its own as AUDT issued for services of $96,774, which is noncash. The other 3,226 AUDT were paid to the Company's PVN.

(5) By August 31, 2027, the Founding PVNs had been admitted to the Network, and the Network went live on that date. That event satisfied the performance obligation on all 70 Units. On that date, the Company recognized revenue of $3,500,000 and cost of revenue of $245,000, and it released the contract liability of $3,500,000 and the deferred Placement Agent compensation of $245,000.
